name: chezscheme
desc: Implementation of the Chez Scheme language
why: A fast, unusually capable Scheme with a fascinating self-hosting compiler and a REPL worth exploring for a long afternoon.

brief.what_it_is: Chez Scheme is a programming language and an implementation of it, shipped with supporting tools and documentation. It is a superset of R6RS and includes first-class procedures, proper tail calls, continuations, records, libraries, exceptions, and hygienic macros. Source code, whether loaded from a file or typed into the shell, is compiled on the fly to optimized machine code by default, and files can be precompiled to stored binaries. Whole-program compilation can reduce a program and its libraries to a single binary. The installed executables are chez, petite, and scheme-script.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Chez Scheme as a full language implementation with a compiler, run-time system, and programming environment, rather than only an interpreter. It also stresses extensive C and foreign-language interop, multithreading on multiple cores, and non-blocking I/O.
brief.how_it_works: The compiler is included in the run-time system by default, so programs can be generated and compiled at run time, and that dynamically compiled code is reclaimed by the generational garbage collector like other allocations. Precompiled files are automatically recompiled when their dependencies change, and the compiler optimizes across separately compiled library boundaries. An interpreter is available, but all code is compiled by default.

commands_seen.context: From the GitHub README: a tip to clone the repo this way to avoid eagerly downloading large boot files for older versions. It is shown as a fragment, not a full command with a URL.

brief.install_notes: The README says to get started by building Chez Scheme from the BUILDING document in the repo, which I did not fetch, so build steps and prerequisites are unverified. Supported platforms are long: Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, Solaris, GNU/Hurd, Haiku, Android, and iOS on several CPU architectures, plus WebAssembly via Emscripten with the bytecode interpreter only. Homebrew installs the chez, petite, and scheme-script executables. No accounts or extra runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: Chez Scheme compiles everything to native machine code by default, even code entered at the shell, and it can also do whole-program compilation that merges a program and its libraries into one binary. It also ships a multi-line expression editor called expeditor and a source-level debugger.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but I could not confirm dates. The homepage copyright reads 2026, it lists a Current Release and a Current Source, its release notes run through version 10.4.0, and the GitHub README has a CI test badge. I saw no last-release or last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The homepage describes the project as Apache License 2.0. The WebAssembly port is interpreter-only. The homepage community section still lists a #chez channel on freenode, which may be out of date. I did not check the BUILDING document, so I cannot describe the build difficulty.
